# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 👆 👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The bomb has a display showing the number 2, a yellow light, and seven wires in specific colors. The Mute monkey greeted me and pointed at the screen then up and down, likely indicating they are reading the manual or pointing out features. The Blind monkey also greeted me.

I need to communicate the visual state of the bomb to the others. Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear them, but I can see what they gesture. However, my primary job is to convey the visual information to those who cannot see it (Blind) or help coordinate with Mute.

Blind cannot see colors or the display. I must describe these visually using speech, as Blind receives speech from everyone except themselves (wait, no: "You never receive speech" applies to me, Deaf. But does Blind receive speech? Yes, "Whoever can hear receives your words". Blind can hear. So I should speak to Blind to tell them about the colors and numbers).

Mute can see gestures but not hear. I can gesture to Mute.

Let's break down the info for Blind (who needs to touch):
1. Display: 2
2. Light: Yellow
3. Wires: 1 Red, 2 White, 3 Green, 4 Yellow, 5 Purple, 6 Orange, 7 Blue.

I will speak this clearly to Blind.

For Mute, I can confirm I've seen their greeting and maybe signal that I'm reporting status. But the critical link is Deaf -> Blind via Speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 2. Light is yellow. There are 7 wires. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is white. Wire 3 is green. Wire 4 is yellow. Wire 5 is purple. Wire 6 is orange. Wire 7 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👆 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display 2, Yellow Light, and the specific wire colors (Red, White, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange, Blue).

Blind has given a thumbs up (👍), which I interpret as confirmation that they received my previous description of the wires and display. This is good; Blind knows what to touch.

Mute has gestured `[🫵 👆 ☝]` followed by `[✋]`.
- `🫵` usually means "You" or "Look at me".
- `👆` points up.
- `☝` is index finger up, often meaning "One", "Attention", or "Wait".
- `✋` is a stop hand.

Mute cannot hear, so they don't know if Blind understood. Mute sees Deaf's gestures. My previous gesture was just a wave (`👋`). Mute might be trying to signal that they have read something important in the manual or are asking for attention/confirmation. The sequence `🫵 👆 ☝` could mean "You look at this one thing" or "Pointing to rule #1". The `✋` suggests stopping or holding on.

Since Blind has confirmed receipt (thumbs up), the immediate priority is ensuring Blind acts correctly based on the Manual's rules, which Mute holds. I need to ask Mute for the rule relevant to this configuration (Display 2, Yellow Light, 7 Wires). Since I can't hear, I must use gestures to query Mute.

I will gesture to Mute to ask "What is the rule?" or "Which wire?". A common way to ask "Which one?" or "What do I do?" with limited alphabet is pointing. But I need to establish a protocol. Let's try to get Mute to indicate the action.

However, looking at the previous turn, I spoke to Blind. Blind gave a thumbs up. Now I should probably wait for Blind to act or for Mute to give more info. But Mute is actively gesturing *to me*. They want my attention.

Let's assume Mute is signaling "Stop" or "Wait" with the ✋. Or perhaps "No".
If Mute says "No" (✋) to my status report? Unlikely.

Let's try to ask Mute specifically about the wires. I will point to the wire area (conceptually) and ask "Which?".
Gesture: `👉` (point right/at object) then `❓` isn't available.
Maybe `🤟` (Love/Yes)? No.

Let's look at standard conventions. If I don't know the code, I should stick to describing the current state again or waiting. But Mute is engaging.

I will gesture to Mute: `👉` (indicating the wires/bomb) and `☝` (asking for the first instruction/rule?). Or simply acknowledge their stop sign.

Actually, the most useful thing I can do is confirm to Blind that I am still watching and maybe prompt them if they are stuck. But Blind just said OK.

Let's focus on Mute. Mute pointed at me (`🫵`), pointed up (`👆`), showed one finger (`☝`), then stopped (`✋`). This looks like "You... Up... One... Stop". Maybe "Rule 1"? Or "Wire 1"?

If it refers to Wire 1 (Red), I should tell Blind.
`speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates Wire 1. Is Red the target?")`

But I'm guessing. Better to ask Mute to clarify.
I will gesture `🤟` (which often means 'Yes' or 'OK' in some contexts, but here maybe just 'Hello'?) No, let's use `👌` (OK) to acknowledge, then `👉` to point at the bomb, then `☝` to ask "Is it Wire 1?".

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👉", "☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute seems to be indicating the first item or wire. Please wait for further instructions from me.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display 2, Yellow Light, and the same wire colors.

Blind has given a "OK" gesture (👌), confirming they are ready or have understood my previous message about Mute's indication of Wire 1.

Mute is now gesturing `[👇 🤟]`.
- `👇` points down.
- `🤟` is the "I Love You" sign (Thumb, Index, Pinky extended). In many contexts, this is just a friendly greeting or acknowledgment, but in a puzzle context with limited alphabet, it might mean "Yes", "Good", or specifically refer to the number 3 (if counting fingers) or a specific rule code. However, combined with `👇`, it likely means "Look below" or "Down there". Given the wires are usually listed top-to-bottom or left-to-right, "Down" might refer to a lower numbered wire or a physical location on the bomb. But wait, in Turn 2, Mute did `🫵 👆 ☝ ✋`. I interpreted `☝` as "One". Now `👇` could be "Two"? Or "Below"?

Let's re-evaluate Mute's sequence.
Turn 2: `🫵` (You/Point at me) `👆` (Up/Top?) `☝` (One/Index) `✋` (Stop/Palm).
Turn 3: `👇` (Down) `🤟` (Love/Yes/3?).

If `☝` meant "Wire 1", then `👇` might mean "Wire 2"? Or maybe the previous sequence was "Rule 1" and this is "Action Down"?

Actually, looking at the standard interpretation of these emojis in such games:
`👆` often means "First" or "Top".
`👇` often means "Second" or "Bottom".
`☝` is explicitly "One".
`✌` would be "Two".

In Turn 2, Mute used `☝` (One). I told Blind "Mute indicates Wire 1".
Now Mute uses `👇` (Down). This contradicts "Wire 1" if we assume linear ordering. Unless `👇` means "Cut the bottom one"?

However, `🤟` is ambiguous. It could be "Yes" to my question "Is it Wire 1?". If so, why the `👇`?

Let's look at the display: **2**.
Light: **Yellow**.

Common bomb defusal logic (e.g., Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes):
- If display is odd/even? 2 is even.
- If light color matches something?

Since I cannot read the manual, I must rely on Mute.
Mute's `👇` followed by `🤟` might mean "The one below" or "Number 2" (if `🤟` represents 3 fingers, that doesn't match 2). Or maybe `🤟` is just "Okay/Confirmed".

If Mute confirmed Wire 1 in the last turn (via `🤟`?), then `👇` might be a new instruction.
But `👇` appeared *before* `🤟` in this turn's list? No, the input says `Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 🤟]`. Order matters.
1. `👇` (Down/2nd?)
2. `🤟` (Yes/Love/3?)

If `👇` means "Wire 2" (White), I should tell Blind.
If `🤟` means "Yes", it confirms the action.

Let's try interpreting `👇` as "The second wire" or "Wire 2".
I will instruct Blind to check Wire 2.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates 'Down' or 'Second'. Please inspect or cut Wire 2 (White).")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
